The image shows a soybean seedling stem/hypocotyl with:
- A distinct dark brown to black discoloration in the upper portion of the stem, extending from the soil line upward
- The lower stem appears healthy green, transitioning through tan/yellow to the dark necrotic upper region
- The tissue appears to be dead and collapsed at the top (shepherd's crook-like bending)
- The lesion is dark, sunken, and dry-looking

This pattern — a dark, sunken canker on the stem at or near the soil line with browning progressing upward — matches **Rhizoctonia**. The reddish-brown to dark brown, firm, dry canker on the hypocotyl/lower stem at the soil line is the hallmark diagnostic feature. The shepherd's crook collapse at the top also fits. The lesion is not water-soaked (ruling out Pythium), and there's no chocolate-brown stem extending well above soil line (ruling out Phytophthora). The dark color and dry canker character are consistent with Rhizoctonia aerial blight/damping-off.
